docs.title: MyFleet documentation portfolio
docs.text:
This site collects technical writing samples for MyFleet, a fictional fleet telematics product line. Every sample is written as if it shipped with a real release, so the pieces link to each other the way they would in a production documentation set.

Fictional product

MyFleet, its hardware, API, and partners are invented. Any resemblance to real products is coincidental.

docs.title: Skills map
docs.text: Area What it shows Samples Product content Print-ready and digital in-box materials, localized MT-100 box insert (EN/ES), Product Availability Matrix User and installation guides Task-based guides for hardware and software, KB and video formats MT-200 installation guide, MT-100 troubleshooting article, video script, Driver App user guide Release communications Customer-ready release notes and a quarterly calendar Release notes 4.2, Q1 2027 release calendar API and OEM documentation Reference, integration guides, changelogs MyFleet API reference, integration guide, OEM Connect setup guide, API changelog Localization Translation workflow, vendor management, quality sign-off EN to ES localization case study, with intake log and LQA scorecard Cross-team collaboration Turning engineering specs into customer language Release 4.2 case study, content readiness checklist Content maintenance Audits, retirement, consistency Content audit and retirement log, style guide

docs.title: How success is measured
docs.text:
Each sample is built to support one or more of these outcomes:

  • On-time delivery: content ships with the product, not after.
  • Translation accuracy: zero critical errors reach the market.
  • API doc quality: fewer support tickets caused by documentation gaps.
  • Content freshness: all materials current within one release cycle.
  • Stakeholder satisfaction: Product and Engineering rate content as release-ready.

docs.title: Glossary
docs.text:
Approved terms for MyFleet content. Translators receive this list as the termbase for every project.

Term Definition Do not use ES (Spain) FR (France) tracker The MT-200 or MT-200 Pro device installed in a vehicle box, unit, black box localizador traceur vehicle Any asset with a tracker installed truck, car (unless specific) vehículo véhicule trip Movement from ignition on to ignition off journey, ride trayecto trajet driver ID The key fob or card a driver uses to log in to a vehicle tag, chip identificación del conductor identifiant conducteur live map The real-time map view in the Dashboard tracking map mapa en tiempo real carte en temps réel geofence A virtual boundary that triggers an alert on entry or exit zone, fence geocerca géorepérage pre-trip check The vehicle inspection a driver completes before a trip walkaround revisión previa al trayecto contrôle avant départ webhook An HTTP callback MyFleet sends when an event occurs push notification webhook webhook API key The secret used to authenticate API requests token (unless OAuth) clave de API clé API OEM Connect Integration that receives data from manufacturer clouds OEM integration (as a name) OEM Connect OEM Connect

Do not translate

Product names (MyFleet, MT-200, Driver App, OEM Connect) and code stay in English in every language.

docs.title: MyFleet product brief
docs.text: MyFleet helps small and mid-sized fleets track vehicles, coach drivers, and cut fuel and maintenance costs. This brief is the single source of truth for product names and capabilities used across the portfolio.

docs.title: Product line
docs.text: Product Type Description MyFleet MT-100 Hardware Plug-and-play tracker for the vehicle's diagnostic (OBD) port. No wiring needed. Green LED shows power; blue LED shows a cellular connection. MyFleet MT-200 Hardware Plug-in vehicle tracker with GPS, 4G LTE-M, and a CAN bus interface. Installs behind the dashboard in about 30 minutes. MyFleet MT-200 Pro Hardware MT-200 with a driver ID reader and two digital inputs for PTO and door sensors. MyFleet Driver App Software (iOS, Android) Lets drivers log in to a vehicle, view assigned jobs, run pre-trip checks, and see driving-style feedback. MyFleet Dashboard Software (web) Live map, trip history, reports, alerts, and user management for fleet managers. MyFleet API Developer platform REST API for vehicles, positions, trips, drivers, and webhooks. MyFleet OEM Connect Partner integration Receives vehicle data directly from manufacturer cloud platforms, with no hardware installation.

docs.title: Audiences
docs.text:
• Fleet managers: use the Dashboard daily. Want quick answers, not theory.
  • Drivers: use the Driver App on the road. Low patience for long text; often non-native English speakers.
  • Installers: fit MT-200 devices. Work in vehicles, often from a phone.
  • Developers and partners: integrate through the API or OEM Connect. Need accurate, complete reference material.

docs.title: Markets and languages
docs.text: MyFleet sells in the UK, Ireland, Spain, France, Belgium, and Mexico. Customer content ships in English (UK), Spanish (Spain), Spanish (Mexico), and French (France).

docs.title: Release cadence
docs.text:
• Software: quarterly feature releases (for example 4.2), with monthly maintenance updates.
  • Firmware: two releases a year, plus security patches as needed.
  • API: versioned (v2 current). Breaking changes get 6 months' notice.

docs.title: MyFleet content style guide
docs.text: This guide keeps MyFleet content consistent across formats, markets, and languages. It also makes translation cheaper and more accurate: shorter, simpler source text means fewer errors.

docs.title: Voice
docs.text:
• Clear over clever. Write for someone reading on a phone in a cab.
  • Direct. Use "you" and the active voice. "Plug the tracker into the OBD port", not "The tracker should be plugged in".
  • Calm. Warnings state the risk and the fix, without drama.

docs.title: Writing for translation
docs.text:
• Keep sentences under 25 words. One instruction per step.
  • Do not use idioms, jokes, or culture-specific references.
  • Use the same term for the same thing every time (see the glossary).
  • Avoid text in images. If you must, keep the editable source file.
  • Leave 30% extra space in print layouts: Spanish and French text runs longer than English.

docs.title: Formatting
docs.text: Element Rule Example UI labels Bold, match the UI exactly Select Save Product names Full name on first use MyFleet Driver App, then Driver App Code, endpoints, values Code format GET /v2/vehicles Numbers Numerals for 10 and above; always numerals with units 5 m, 12 V Dates Day month year in prose; ISO 8601 in data 9 November 2026; 2026-11-09

docs.title: Procedures
docs.text:
1. Start with a one-line goal ("To add a driver, ...").
  2. List prerequisites before step 1.
  3. Start each step with a verb.
  4. End with a result the user can check ("The vehicle appears on the live map").

docs.title: Admonitions
docs.text:
• Note: helpful extra information.
  • Important: something that can cause a task to fail.
  • Warning: a risk of injury, vehicle damage, or data loss. Use sparingly.

docs.title: Spelling
docs.text: Source content uses UK English to match the primary market.

docs.title: MyFleet API changelog
docs.text: All notable API changes. We follow semantic versioning: breaking changes only in a new major version, with at least 6 months' notice.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• data_source field on Vehicle (tracker or oem_connect), so you can tell where a vehicle's data comes from.
  • vehicle.defect_reported webhook event, sent when a driver reports a defect in a pre-trip check.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text: • GET /trips now accepts ranges up to 31 days (was 7 days).

docs.title: Deprecated
docs.text: • The driver_name field on Trip is deprecated. Use driver_id and GET /drivers/{id} instead. It will be removed in v3, no earlier than 2027-06-01.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text: • GET /vehicles sometimes returned a next_cursor on the last page. It now returns null.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• geofence.entered and geofence.exited webhook events.
  • heading field on Position.

docs.title: Integration guide: Sync trips to your system
docs.text:
This guide shows you how to send completed MyFleet trips to your own system, such as a payroll or job-costing tool. By the end, your system receives each trip within seconds of the vehicle stopping.

You need: a MyFleet account with the API access add-on, admin rights, and a public HTTPS endpoint. Time: about 1 hour.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
1. A vehicle's ignition turns off and MyFleet closes the trip.
  2. MyFleet sends a trip.ended webhook to your endpoint.
  3. Your endpoint verifies the signature and stores the trip.
  4. Once a night, your system calls GET /trips to catch anything it missed.

docs.title: Step 1: Create an API key
docs.text:
1. In the MyFleet Dashboard, go to Settings > API keys.
  2. Select Create key, name it (for example payroll-sync), and select Read access.
  3. Copy the key. You won't see it again.

docs.title: Step 2: Test your key
docs.text:
curl https://api.myfleet.example/v2/vehicles?limit=1 \
  -H "X-API-Key: YOUR_API_KEY"

A 200 response with one vehicle means the key works.

docs.title: Step 3: Subscribe to trip events
docs.text:
curl -X POST https://api.myfleet.example/v2/webhooks \
  -H "X-API-Key: YOUR_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"url": "https://example.com/myfleet/events", "events": ["trip.ended"]}'

Store the secret from the response.

docs.title: Step 4: Verify webhook signatures
docs.text:
Each webhook has a MyFleet-Signature header: an HMAC-SHA256 of the raw request body, using your secret. Reject any request where the signature doesn't match.

import hmac, hashlib

def is_valid(raw_body: bytes, header: str, secret: str) -> bool:
    expected = hmac.new(secret.encode(), raw_body, hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()
    return hmac.compare_digest(expected, header)

Important

Use the raw body bytes. Parsing and re-serializing the JSON changes the bytes and the check fails.

Respond with 2xx within 10 seconds. If you don't, MyFleet retries 5 times over 24 hours.

docs.title: Step 5: Backfill missed trips
docs.text:
Webhooks can be missed during outages. Run a nightly job that requests the last 24 hours and stores any trip IDs you don't have:

curl "https://api.myfleet.example/v2/trips?from=2026-11-08T00:00:00Z&to=2026-11-09T00:00:00Z" \
  -H "X-API-Key: YOUR_API_KEY"

Use the trip id to avoid duplicates.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Add geofence.entered events to log site arrivals.
  • See the full API reference and the changelog.

docs.title: Set up MyFleet OEM Connect
docs.text: OEM Connect brings vehicle data straight from the manufacturer's cloud into MyFleet, with no tracker to install. Use it for new vehicles from supported manufacturers, or for mixed fleets where some vehicles already have built-in telematics.

docs.title: Supported data
docs.text:
Data Tracker (MT-200) OEM Connect Position and speed ✓ every 15 s ✓ every 60 s (varies by manufacturer) Ignition on/off ✓ ✓ Odometer With CAN ✓ Fuel level / battery charge With CAN ✓ Driver ID MT-200 Pro only ✗ Harsh driving events ✓ Some manufacturers

Check supported manufacturers and models for each market in the Product Availability Matrix.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• MyFleet admin rights.
  • The VIN of each vehicle.
  • Permission from the vehicle owner to share data. In most markets, the manufacturer asks the owner to confirm in their own app or portal.

docs.title: Step 1: Add the manufacturer connection
docs.text:
1. In the MyFleet Dashboard, go to Settings > OEM Connect.
  2. Select Add connection and choose the manufacturer.
  3. Accept the data-sharing terms.

docs.title: Step 2: Add vehicles
docs.text:
1. Select Add vehicles.
  2. Enter VINs one by one, or upload a CSV file with one VIN per line.
  3. Select Request access.

Each vehicle shows Pending consent until the owner approves.

docs.title: Step 3: Get owner consent
docs.text:
The manufacturer sends a consent request to the registered owner. When the owner approves, the status changes to Active (usually within 24 hours).

Leased vehicles

For leased vehicles, the leasing company is the registered owner. Send them the VIN list and ask them to approve the requests.

docs.title: Step 4: Check data is arriving
docs.text:
1. Open the live map and find the vehicle.
  2. Check the data source icon shows OEM.
  3. Through the API, the vehicle's data_source is oem_connect.

docs.title: Use cases
docs.text:
• No-install onboarding: get new vans on the map the day they're delivered.
  • Electric fleets: use the manufacturer's battery data for charging reports.
  • Mixed fleets: combine trackers and OEM data in one map and one API.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Status Meaning What to do Pending consent for more than 7 days Owner hasn't approved Ask the owner to check the manufacturer app Not eligible Model or year not supported Install an MT-200 instead Data delayed Manufacturer cloud is slow Normal delays are up to 5 minutes; check the status page if longer

docs.title: MyFleet API reference
docs.text: Version: 2.4.0 · Base URL: https://api.myfleet.example/v2 The full machine-readable spec is in openapi.yaml. Import it into Postman or any OpenAPI tool.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
Send your API key in the X-API-Key header with every request. Create keys in the MyFleet Dashboard under Settings > API keys.

curl https://api.myfleet.example/v2/vehicles \
  -H "X-API-Key: YOUR_API_KEY"

docs.title: Rate limits
docs.text: You can send up to 600 requests per minute per key. If you go over, you get 429 Too Many Requests with a Retry-After header that says how many seconds to wait.

docs.title: Pagination
docs.text: List endpoints return up to limit items (default 50, max 200) and a next_cursor. Pass next_cursor as the cursor parameter to get the next page. When next_cursor is null, you have everything.

docs.title: List vehicles
docs.text:
GET /vehicles

Parameter In Type Required Description limit query integer No Items per page, 1 to 200. Default 50. cursor query string No Cursor from the previous page. group_id query string No Return only vehicles in this group. 200 OK
{
  "data": [
    {
      "id": "veh_8f2k1",
      "registration": "AB12 CDE",
      "vin": "WF0XXXTTGXKA12345",
      "group_id": "grp_north",
      "data_source": "tracker"
    }
  ],
  "next_cursor": "eyJpZCI6MTIzfQ"
}

docs.title: Get latest position
docs.text:
GET /vehicles/{vehicle_id}/positions/latest

Returns the most recent position, whether it came from an MT-200 tracker or from OEM Connect.

200 OK
{
  "vehicle_id": "veh_8f2k1",
  "latitude": 53.4808,
  "longitude": -2.2426,
  "speed_kmh": 48,
  "heading": 270,
  "ignition": true,
  "recorded_at": "2026-11-09T08:14:03Z"
}

docs.title: List trips
docs.text:
GET /trips

Parameter In Type Required Description from query date-time Yes Start of range, ISO 8601 in UTC. to query date-time Yes End of range. Maximum 31 days after from. vehicle_id query string No Return trips for one vehicle only.

Note

driver_id is null when nobody was logged in to the vehicle during the trip.

docs.title: Create a webhook subscription
docs.text:
POST /webhooks

Request body
{
  "url": "https://example.com/myfleet/events",
  "events": ["trip.ended", "geofence.entered"]
}

The response includes a secret. It's shown only once, so store it securely. See Verify webhook signatures.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text: Status Code Meaning What to do 400 invalid_range The time range is longer than 31 days Split the request into smaller ranges 401 invalid_api_key Key missing, wrong, or revoked Check the X-API-Key header 404 not_found The resource doesn't exist or isn't in your account Check the ID 429 rate_limited Too many requests Wait for Retry-After seconds

docs.title: MyFleet Driver App user guide
docs.text: The MyFleet Driver App lets you log in to a vehicle, see your jobs, complete pre-trip checks, and review your driving. Version: 4.2 · Platforms: iOS 16 and later, Android 11 and later

docs.title: Sign in
docs.text:
1. Open the Driver App.
  2. Enter the email address and temporary password from your fleet manager.
  3. Create a new password when asked.

Note

Forgot your password? Select Forgot password on the sign-in screen. If you have no email access, ask your fleet manager to reset it.

docs.title: Log in to a vehicle
docs.text:
To link your trips to you, log in to the vehicle before you drive.

With a driver IDIn the app

Hold your driver ID against the reader on the dashboard. The reader beeps twice and the app shows the vehicle name.

  1. Select Vehicles.
  2. Select the vehicle's registration number, or scan the QR code on the windscreen sticker.
  3. Select Log in.

docs.title: Complete a pre-trip check
docs.text:
Your fleet may require a pre-trip check before your first trip of the day.

  1. On the home screen, select Start pre-trip check.
  2. Check each item and select OK or Defect.
  3. For a defect, take a photo and add a short description.
  4. Select Submit.

Result: your fleet manager gets the report straight away. If you reported a defect that makes the vehicle unsafe, don't drive. Wait for your fleet manager's instructions.

docs.title: View your jobs
docs.text:
Select Jobs to see today's jobs in order. Select a job to see the address, contact, and notes. Select Navigate to open your maps app.

When you arrive, select Arrived. When you finish, select Complete and collect a signature if the job needs one.

docs.title: Check your driving score
docs.text:
Select My driving to see a score from 0 to 100 based on:

  • harsh braking
  • harsh acceleration
  • speeding
  • idling

Tap any score to see the events that lowered it, with time and location.

docs.title: Privacy
docs.text: When you log out of a vehicle, or turn on Private mode (if your fleet allows it), the app stops linking trips to you. Your fleet manager can see your trips, jobs, and score, but not your phone's location outside work.

docs.title: MT-100 vehicle does not appear in the MyFleet Dashboard
docs.text: Applies to: MyFleet MT-100 · Article type: Troubleshooting Article ID: KB-0142 · Last reviewed: 9 November 2026 (Release 4.2)

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: If your vehicle does not appear in the MyFleet Dashboard after installing the MT-100 tracker, follow the troubleshooting steps below to identify and resolve the issue.

docs.title: Possible causes
docs.text:
The vehicle may not appear on the platform for the following reasons:

  • The MT-100 tracker is not properly connected to the vehicle's diagnostic port.
  • The tracker is not receiving power.
  • The tracker has not established a cellular network connection.
  • The data transmission period has not elapsed.
  • The vehicle is not associated with the correct customer account.

docs.title: 1. Check the tracker connection
docs.text: Ensure that the MT-100 is firmly connected to the vehicle's diagnostic port.

docs.title: 2. Check the power indicator
docs.text:
Check the tracker's LED indicator. A green LED indicates that the tracker is receiving power.

If the green LED is not illuminated, check that the vehicle ignition is switched on. If the indicator remains off, contact Technical Support.

docs.title: 3. Check the cellular network connection
docs.text:
Check the tracker's LED indicator. A blue LED indicates that the tracker has established a cellular network connection.

If the blue LED is not illuminated, verify that the tracker is properly connected and receiving power. If the issue persists, contact Technical Support.

docs.title: 4. Allow time for data transmission
docs.text: Once the cellular network connection is established, allow up to five minutes for vehicle data to appear in the MyFleet Dashboard. After five minutes, refresh the Dashboard and check whether the vehicle is visible.

docs.title: 5. Verify the customer account
docs.text: Check that the vehicle is associated with the correct customer account. If you cannot verify the account association, contact your fleet administrator or Technical Support.

docs.title: Contact Technical Support
docs.text:
If the vehicle still does not appear in the MyFleet Dashboard after completing the troubleshooting steps, contact Technical Support through the approved support channel.

To help the support team investigate the issue, provide:

  • Vehicle identification or fleet reference.
  • MT-100 tracker identification, if available.
  • Description of the issue.
  • Current LED indicator status.
  • Installation date and time.
  • Relevant screenshots of the MyFleet Dashboard.

Note

Include photographs of the tracker installation where relevant. Only take photographs when it is safe to do so.

docs.title: Install the MyFleet MT-200 tracker
docs.text:
Applies to: MT-200, MT-200 Pro · Time: about 30 minutes · Skill level: trained installer Article ID: KB-0101 · Last reviewed: 9 November 2026 (Release 4.2)

This article explains how to install an MT-200 tracker in a vehicle and confirm it reports to MyFleet. A video version is available in the MyFleet video library.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
You need:

  • an MT-200 or MT-200 Pro tracker and its wiring harness (in the box)
  • the vehicle's registration number and VIN
  • the MyFleet Installer app, signed in with your installer account
  • a multimeter and cable ties

Disconnect the vehicle battery

Disconnect the negative battery terminal before you connect the power wires. A short circuit can damage the vehicle's electronics.

Check vehicle compatibility

Electric and hybrid vehicles may need the CAN bus adapter (part MT-ACC-04). Check the Product Availability Matrix before you go to site.

docs.title: Step 1: Choose a mounting location
docs.text:
1. Find a location behind the dashboard, at least 30 cm from the radio and airbag modules.
  2. Make sure the top of the tracker (the side with the label) faces the windscreen. The GPS antenna needs a clear view of the sky.

docs.title: Step 2: Connect the wiring
docs.text:
Wire Connect to Notes Red Permanent 12/24 V supply Use the 2 A fuse in the harness Black Vehicle ground Bare metal chassis point White Ignition (switched) supply Check with the multimeter: 0 V with ignition off Green / Yellow CAN high / CAN low Optional. Only for fuel and odometer data
  1. Connect the black wire first, then the red, then the white.
  2. Reconnect the vehicle battery.
  3. Plug the harness into the tracker. The LED flashes amber while it searches for a network.

docs.title: Step 3: Register the tracker
docs.text:
1. In the Installer app, select New installation.
  2. Scan the QR code on the tracker label.
  3. Enter the vehicle's registration number and VIN, then select Register.

docs.title: Step 4: Test the installation
docs.text:
1. Turn on the ignition.
  2. Wait for the LED to turn solid green (up to 3 minutes).
  3. In the Installer app, select Run test. The app checks GPS, network, and ignition signals.

Result: the app shows Installation passed, and the vehicle appears on the live map in the MyFleet Dashboard.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
LED Meaning What to do Off No power Check the red and black wires and the fuse Flashing amber after 5 minutes No network Move the vehicle outside; check the SIM is active in the Installer app Flashing red No GPS fix Make sure the label side faces the windscreen and is not under metal

Still stuck? Contact installer support from the Installer app (Help > Contact support) and include the tracker serial number.

docs.title: Video script: Installing the MT-200 in 4 minutes
docs.text:
Format: screen and hands-on footage, voice-over · Length: about 4 minutes Source article: KB-0101 · Subtitles: EN, ES, FR

For translators

Voice-over lines are kept under 15 words so subtitles fit two lines. On-screen text is kept as separate layers so it can be localized without re-editing.

# Time Visual Voice-over On-screen text 1 0:00 MyFleet logo, van in a workshop In this video, you'll install a MyFleet MT-200 tracker and test it. Install the MT-200 2 0:08 Items laid on a bench You need the tracker, the harness, a multimeter, and the Installer app. What you need 3 0:20 Close-up: hand removing battery terminal First, disconnect the negative battery terminal. ⚠ Disconnect the battery 4 0:30 Behind dashboard, pointing to location Mount the tracker behind the dashboard, label side up, away from airbags. 30 cm from airbags 5 0:50 Wires being connected, colour callouts Connect black to ground, red to permanent power, white to ignition. Black · Red · White 6 1:40 Multimeter on ignition wire Check the ignition wire reads zero volts with the ignition off. 0 V = ignition off 7 2:00 Battery reconnected, LED flashing amber Reconnect the battery. The amber light means it's searching for a network. 8 2:20 Phone screen: scanning QR code In the Installer app, select New installation and scan the QR code. New installation 9 2:50 Ignition on, LED turns green Turn on the ignition and wait for a solid green light. Solid green = connected 10 3:10 Phone: Run test, "Installation passed" Select Run test. When you see Installation passed, you're done. Installation passed ✓ 11 3:40 Dashboard live map with new vehicle The vehicle now appears on the live map. 12 3:50 End card with KB link For troubleshooting, see the full article in the MyFleet knowledge base. help.myfleet.example/KB-0101

docs.title: Production notes
docs.text:
• Review: hardware engineering signs off on wiring footage before the edit is locked.
  • Shot list: shots 3, 5, and 6 need close-ups with a clear background for colour visibility.
  • Accessibility: captions burned off (sidecar files) so each language can be loaded.

docs.title: Case study: Localizing the MT-100 launch from English to Spanish
docs.text:
Scope: box insert, knowledge base article KB-0142, Driver App release strings · Markets: Spain Role: technical writer and localization owner · Result: shipped on launch day with zero critical errors

Portfolio sample

MyFleet is fictional. This case study shows the process I would run, using realistic numbers and decisions.

docs.title: The challenge
docs.text:
The MT-100 was launching in Spain on the same day as Release 4.2. Three things had to be ready in Spanish at launch:

  • the printed box insert, which had a print deadline 3 weeks before launch
  • the troubleshooting article KB-0142
  • 140 new Driver App strings for defect alerts

The earlier MT-200 launch had shipped its Spanish insert 2 weeks late, and one term ("caja negra" for tracker) caused customer confusion.

docs.title: 1. Fixed the source first
docs.text:
Before sending anything to translation, I edited the English source against the style guide:

  • cut average sentence length from 21 to 13 words
  • replaced 3 different words for the device ("unit", "box", "device") with one: tracker
  • removed an idiom ("plug and play, no sweat")
  • confirmed timings (3 minutes for LEDs, 5 minutes for the map) with hardware engineering

Why: every unclear source sentence becomes an unclear sentence in every language, and costs money to fix in each one.

docs.title: 2. Updated the termbase
docs.text: I added 6 new terms to the glossary with approved Spanish translations and loaded them into the translation platform so the vendor saw them as mandatory. Localizador replaced caja negra.

docs.title: 3. Intake and routing
docs.text:
Request Requested by Content type Words Route Due LOC-231 Hardware product Box insert (XLIFF from InDesign) 180 Vendor A, print priority Day 5 LOC-232 Support KB-0142 420 Vendor A Day 10 LOC-233 Engineering Driver App strings (JSON) 960 Vendor A + in-market review Day 12

Translation memory matched 38% of the words from earlier projects, which cut cost and kept wording consistent with the MT-200 docs.

docs.title: 4. Review cycle
docs.text:
1. Vendor translation and self-review in the translation platform.
  2. Automated QA: terminology, numbers, tags, and untranslated segments.
  3. In-market review by a Spain-based fleet support agent, who checked that the instructions matched real vehicles.
  4. My review of the box insert in context (the PDF proof, not just the strings), because truncation and line breaks only show up in layout.
  5. Sign-off using the scorecard below.

docs.title: 5. Quality scorecard (LQA)
docs.text:
Category Critical Major Minor Accuracy 0 0 1 Terminology 0 0 0 Language (grammar, spelling) 0 0 2 Style and register 0 1 0 Layout (truncation, line breaks) 0 0 1 Total 0 1 4

Pass rule: 0 critical, at most 2 major per 1,000 words. All issues fixed before release.

docs.title: Examples of decisions
docs.text: English source First translation Final Why it changed Turn the ignition off. Apague la ignición. Apague el contacto. Ignición is a literal calque; drivers in Spain say contacto. Push the MT-100 firmly into the port until it stops. Empuje firmemente el MT-100 en el puerto hasta que se detenga. Introduzca el MT-100 en el puerto hasta el fondo. Shorter, natural, and fits the card without shrinking the font. Your vehicle appears on the live map. Tu vehículo aparece en el mapa en vivo. Su vehículo aparecerá en el mapa en tiempo real. Formal usted for hardware docs; approved glossary term. Defect reported Defecto reportado Avería notificada Reportar is a common anglicism; avería is what fleet managers in Spain use. (Mexico variant: Falla reportada.)

docs.title: Results
docs.text: Measure MT-200 launch (before) MT-100 launch (after) Spanish content ready on launch day No (2 weeks late) Yes Critical errors reaching market 1 0 Translation cost per word (with TM) baseline 22% lower Spanish support tickets about installation, first month 41 17

docs.title: What I'd do next

docs.title: Retirement rules
docs.text:
A page is retired when any of these is true:

  • the product or feature has reached end of life
  • it has had fewer than 20 views in 6 months and no support ticket links to it
  • its content is fully covered by another page (merge instead, and redirect)

Retired pages are redirected, never just deleted, so links from old emails, PDFs, and printed QR codes still work. Translations are retired at the same time as the English page.

docs.title: MT-100 quick-start box insert
docs.text: This sample is the printed quick-start card that ships in the MT-100 box. It is written for a driver or fleet manager with no installation training, so it uses short steps and plain words.

docs.title: Print specification
docs.text:
Item Value Part number MF-DOC-100-QSG rev. B Format A6 (105 × 148 mm), folded from A5, double-sided Colour 2 colour (black + MyFleet blue, Pantone 2728 C) Paper 120 gsm uncoated, FSC certified Bleed / safe area 3 mm bleed, 5 mm safe area Languages EN (UK), ES (Spain) on one card, one language per side Text expansion Layout leaves 30% extra space for Spanish Artwork source MF-DOC-100-QSG_revB.indd, text exported to XLIFF for translation Digital version Same content as an accessible PDF and a knowledge base page Linked to release Firmware 3.8 / Release 4.2

Why it's built this way

One language per side keeps the card short and lets the same layout serve EN/ES markets now and FR later. Icons carry the meaning of each step, so the card still works if a reader skips the text.

docs.title: Side A: English
docs.text:
Rendered card (EN)Source text (Markdown) 
# MyFleet MT-100 · Quick start
**Set up your tracker in 5 minutes. No tools needed.**
**In the box:** MT-100 tracker · this card

1. **Find the diagnostic port**
   Look under the dashboard, near the steering column. The port has 16 pins.
2. **Plug in the tracker**
   Turn the ignition off. Push the MT-100 firmly into the port until it stops.
3. **Turn on the ignition**
   Green light = power is on. Blue light = connected to the mobile network.
   Both lights should be on within 3 minutes.
4. **Check your vehicle in MyFleet**
   Open the MyFleet Dashboard or Driver App. Your vehicle appears on the live map within 5 minutes.

> Safety: Do not install the tracker while driving. Make sure it does not touch the pedals or block your legs.

Vehicle not showing? help.myfleet.example/KB-0142

docs.title: MyFleet MT-100 · Quick start
docs.text:
Set up your tracker in 5 minutes. No tools needed.

In the box: MT-100 tracker · this card

1. Find the diagnostic port Look under the dashboard, near the steering column. The port has 16 pins. Not sure where it is? Check your vehicle handbook for "OBD port".

2. Plug in the tracker Turn the ignition off. Push the MT-100 firmly into the port until it stops.

3. Turn on the ignition Wait for the lights:

Light Meaning 🟢 Green Power is on 🔵 Blue Connected to the mobile network

Both lights should be on within 3 minutes.

4. Check your vehicle in MyFleet Open the MyFleet Dashboard or Driver App. Your vehicle appears on the live map within 5 minutes.

⚠ Safety: Do not install the tracker while driving. Make sure it does not touch the pedals or block your legs.

Vehicle not showing? Scan the QR code or go to help.myfleet.example/KB-0142

docs.title: MyFleet MT-100 · Guía rápida
docs.text:
Instale su localizador en 5 minutos. No necesita herramientas.

Contenido de la caja: localizador MT-100 · esta tarjeta

1. Busque el puerto de diagnóstico Mire debajo del salpicadero, cerca de la columna de dirección. El puerto tiene 16 pines. ¿No sabe dónde está? Busque «puerto OBD» en el manual del vehículo.

2. Conecte el localizador Apague el contacto. Introduzca el MT-100 en el puerto hasta el fondo.

3. Encienda el contacto Espere a que se enciendan las luces:

Luz Significado 🟢 Verde El localizador recibe alimentación 🔵 Azul Conectado a la red móvil

Las dos luces deberían encenderse en menos de 3 minutos.

4. Compruebe su vehículo en MyFleet Abra el MyFleet Dashboard o la Driver App. Su vehículo aparecerá en el mapa en tiempo real en menos de 5 minutos.

⚠ Seguridad: No instale el localizador mientras conduce. Asegúrese de que no toque los pedales ni moleste a las piernas.

¿No aparece el vehículo? Escanee el código QR o visite help.myfleet.example/es/KB-0142

[Código QR] MF-DOC-100-QSG rev. B · © MyFleet

docs.title: MyFleet Release 4.2 release notes
docs.text: Release date: 17 November 2026 · Rollout: gradual over 2 weeks, all markets Applies to: Dashboard, Driver App 4.2, MT-200 firmware 3.8, API 2.4

docs.title: Defect alerts from pre-trip checks
docs.text: When a driver reports a defect in the Driver App, fleet managers now get an alert straight away, by email or in the Dashboard. Why it matters: unsafe vehicles get fixed before they go back on the road. Set it up: Settings > Alerts > New alert > Defect reported.

docs.title: OEM Connect for more manufacturers
docs.text: OEM Connect now supports two more manufacturers in the UK, Spain, and France. See the Product Availability Matrix for models.

docs.title: Longer trip reports in the API
docs.text: Developers can now request up to 31 days of trips in one call. See the API changelog.

docs.title: Improvements
docs.text:
• Dashboard: the live map loads up to 40% faster for fleets with more than 500 vehicles.
  • Driver App: you can attach up to 5 photos to a defect report (was 1).
  • MT-200 firmware 3.8: faster GPS fix after the vehicle has been parked for a long time.

docs.title: Fixes
docs.text:
• Trip distances no longer show as 0 km when the trip crosses midnight.
  • The Driver App no longer signs you out after an iOS update.

docs.title: Changes to be aware of
docs.text:
Action needed for API users

The driver_name field is deprecated and will be removed in API v3. If your integration uses it, switch to driver_id.

docs.title: Firmware update
docs.text: MT-200 trackers update over the air when parked with the ignition off. You don't need to do anything. To check, open the vehicle in the Dashboard and look for Firmware 3.8 under Device.

docs.title: Languages
docs.text: These release notes are available in English, Spanish (Spain and Mexico), and French.
